headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 9 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.7 (95% CI: 0.51–0.95), suggesting that dairy is associated with a lower risk of bladder cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 81.22%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

cases.excerpt: To examine the relation of the total intake of fluids and the types of beverages to the risk of bladder cancer, we conducted a hospital based case-control study with 130 newly diagnosed bladder cancer patients and the same number of matched controls.

effect_size.excerpt: Multivariate logistic regression model showed consumption of: soda (OR=8.32; 95%CI=3.18-21.76), coffee (OR=1.46; 95%CI=1.05-2.01) and spirits (OR=1.15; 95%CI=1.04-1.28) as statistically significant risk factors, while mineral water (OR=0.52; 95%CI=0.34-0.79), skim milk (OR=0.38; 95%CI=0.16-0.91), yogurt (OR=0.34; 95%CI=0.12-0.97) and frequency of daily urination (OR=0.27; 95%CI=0.18-0.41) were statistically significant protective variables.

effect_size.excerpt: After adjusting confounding factors, it was observed that the odds of bladder cancer were significantly lower in the second and last tertiles (T) of total peptide intake from dairy products compared to the first tertile (T<sub>2</sub>: odds ratio (OR) = 0.285; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.116-0.699, T<sub>3</sub>: OR = 0.130; 95% CI: 0.032-0.527). Additionally, in the adjusted model, a significant inverse association was found between other dairy-derived peptides and the odds of bladder cancer.

design.excerpt: We conducted this case-control study to examine the association between dairy-derived BPs and bladder cancer.

continent.excerpt: conducted in three referral hospitals in Tehran, Iran

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary intake was assessed using a validated 168-item Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ). Intake of BPs was estimated based on dairy product consumption recorded in the FFQ.
